commits.message:
docs(console): print's string-truncation count sits after the closing quote (rich-pretty-efq)

PRINT_DATA_BOUNDS' header and docs/console.md both still described maxString's
+N as inside the quotes, the form this branch removed.

fix(pretty): maxString's dropped count sits outside the closing quote (rich-pretty-efq)

Pretty cut a long string and appended "+N" before JSON.stringify, so the
count was quoted as the string's own content — "Field b+316" — and copying
the rendered value yielded a string the program never held. Quote the kept
prefix first and annotate after it: "Field b"+316, the same way maxLength's
"... +N" sits beside the kept entries rather than inside the last one.

The ticket's second instance (Map/Set maxLength truncating silently) is
already fixed on master by the shared `elided()` marker every container
kind goes through; verified, nothing to change.

fix(pretty): a container's compact try is charged for the key it sits under (#148)

Merging: full review sequence (high → medium → high → medium → low) complete, all findings addressed or routed to follow-up tickets, working tree clean.

The "Review" (AI Code Review) CI check shows FAILURE / mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE — verified via `gh run view --log-failed`: it's the CI job's own Claude subscription hitting its rate limit ("You've hit your limit · resets Sep 18, 11am (UTC)"), not a code finding. Same infra issue seen on PR #147. This repo has no required status checks; UNSTABLE ≠ blocked.

Follow-up tickets filed (not folded into this PR — different bug class / different fix shape each):
- rich-pretty-xms.tmf — Pretty's self-describing "text" shape (Error/custom toString) and bare scalars never go through any compact-fit budget at all.
- rich-pretty-xms.0l4 — the expand branch's own opening-bracket line (`key: Set {`) is emitted with no width check against the column it lands at.
